A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CARES and contain readable text, equations, figures, and tables supporting reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains a two-page appendix, which was included in the comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, accuracy–latency measurements, and ablations of feature extraction, resolution selection, and label smoothing.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, CARES-AR results, and appendix latency measurements and resolution distributions.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds a second selector implementation: Granite-Docling-258M adapted with LoRA and next-token supervision over dedicated resolution tokens. CARES-AR interpolates first-step token probabilities into a resolution. This substantially expands the proposed architecture and training procedure; the original SmolVLM classifier and labeling rule remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Table 2 expands evaluation from five to nine datasets, adding MMMU, RealWorldQA, InfoVQA, and MathVista while retaining the original benchmarks. This substantially broadens evaluated data coverage, although the new datasets' composition and task requirements are not described. The four training datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds CARES-AR as an alternative selector alongside CARES in the Granite-Vision and InternVL3 comparisons. Existing native-model baselines and fixed-resolution controls are retained; no evaluated external token-compression baseline is added.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a separate CARES-AR training protocol: three epochs, learning rate 1e-5, and batch size 64. New Table 7 measures latency over 100 DocVQA examples at batch size 1 on H100. The original classifier settings remain unchanged; metrics and splits for the four added benchmarks are unspecified.

E4.justification: The appendix extends latency analysis to two smaller downstream models and examines task-dependent routing through new Ai2D, DocVQA, and SeedBench-2 resolution histograms. These supplement the retained ablations in Tables 3–6. The OCRBench histogram in Figure 5 repeats existing Figure 3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Table 7's average over 100 examples specifies the evaluation sample size, not repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial benchmark and CARES-AR results, including an InternVL3 SeedBench-2 tradeoff: CARES-AR scores 0.72 with 84% compute savings versus CARES at 0.79 with 44% savings. Table 7 newly reports Qwen2.5-VL-7B native/CARES latency of 435.7/270.1 ms. Retained benchmark scores are rounded more coarsely; nine-benchmark averages replace five-benchmark averages and are not directly comparable.

T1.justification: The problem definition, sufficiency criterion, interpolation equation, and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. The autoregressive implementation introduces no new formal derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction newly presents CARES as independent of predictor architecture and explicitly includes an autoregressive instantiation. The original contribution list and main claims about preserving performance, reducing compute, and leaving the target VLM unchanged are retained.

C2.justification: The appendix adds task-specific interpretations: low Ai2D resolutions suggest coarse visual requirements, high SeedBench-2 resolutions suggest finer recognition requirements, and broader DocVQA/OCRBench distributions suggest mixed detail demands. It also connects the new latency measurements to practical inference gains. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link, CARES-AR implementation and training details—including rank-8 LoRA, resolution-token mapping, and one-token generation—and hardware and sampling information for Table 7. Original implementation disclosures remain. The PDFs establish the added link, not what resources are available through it.

R1.justification: v2 adds Auer et al.'s Docling technical report to support the new Granite-Docling instantiation. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to token sparsification, flexible token budgets, and adaptive resolution methods otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to introductory additions, renaming Section 3.3 to Model Instantiations, new architecture and training paragraphs, and three appendix subsections. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained, without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned to compare conventional and CARES pipelines. Table 2 gains four benchmark groups and CARES-AR rows, with smaller text and coarser numerical formatting. New Table 7 and Figures 4–5 substantially expand the displays; Figure 5 includes a repeated OCRBench panel, while existing figures and tables also shift positions.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's single latency plot, Table 7 strengthens practical-efficiency evidence with measurements for two smaller models and explicit hardware and sampling details. The additional routing analyses and alternative selector also help assess generality. These gains are limited by incomplete integration: the abstract and evaluation setup still describe five benchmarks, and metrics for the four added datasets are not specified.
